name: Idiopathic Avascular Necrosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and imaging findings

criteria.description: Progressive joint pain localized to affected site without history of trauma or known risk factors
Radiologic evidence of bone ischemia and necrosis on MRI or X-ray
Absence of identifiable secondary causes such as corticosteroid use, alcohol abuse, or trauma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical symptoms plus imaging evidence of avascular necrosis with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; biopsy rarely required

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized deep joint pain exacerbated by weight-bearing
searchTerms: deep joint pain worsened by walking
joint ache when standing or walking

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced range of motion in affected joint

common.symptomName: Joint stiffness especially in the morning
Limping gait when lower extremity joints are involved
searchTerms: limping due to joint pain in legs
altered gait from lower limb pain
grating or crackling sound in joints
loss of muscle bulk by joint
symptoms of secondary joint wear and tear

rare.symptomName: Systemic constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: general symptoms like low fever and fatigue

laboratory: Exclusion of infectious or autoimmune markers
imaging: MRI showing bone marrow edema and subchondral signal changes
X-ray demonstrating sclerosis, subchondral radiolucent crescent sign, and eventual collapse
CT scan may show cortical bone collapse
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified in idiopathic cases
other: Histopathology (rarely performed) shows dead bone with empty lacunae and marrow necrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of known risk factors such as corticosteroid use or alcohol abuse
History of trauma or systemic disease
Acute onset with systemic signs of infection
Elevated inflammatory markers and positive joint fluid cultures
Gradual onset with joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation on imaging
Lack of bone marrow edema typical of avascular necrosis

redFlags: Severe unremitting pain despite conservative management
Signs of joint infection or systemic illness
references: Moya-Angeler J, et al. Avascular necrosis of the femoral head: pathophysiology and current concepts of treatment. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2015.
Mont MA, et al. Nontraumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head: ten years later. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2006.
